transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-04-08 10:00 PDT | Duration 62m | Host: Evan Scott | Attendees: Evan, Priya, Daniel, Maya, Oliver + all employees

[00:00] Evan: Alright good morning everyone, thanks for joining the April all-hands. A bunch to cover today, quick FYI we'll keep Q&A to the end but drop questions in the Q&A panel or the chat, we'll try to get to as many as we can.

[00:18] Priya: Quick housekeeping, slides are up, link in chat, recording will be posted after. We'll start with OKRs and then product, infra, hiring.

[00:35] Evan: First up, topline — we're tracking to plan for Q2 revenue and usage, thanks to the team for shipping the new batching improvements. We saw a 12% reduction in e2e token cost for a subset of customers in early canary. Not perfect, the metric is noisy but it's trending right.

[01:02] Daniel: To add, the batching runtime patch reduced tail latency for 8k sequences in our internal tests. There were a couple of regressions in small sequence throughput we squashed this week. Still debugging a nv-interop issue, might be a kernel selection bug.

[01:31] Employee 1: sorry can you repeat the nv interop bit?

[01:35] Daniel: Yeah, nv-interop, basically some GPU kernel selector path didn't pick the low-latency kernel for certain shapes, leads to a slight spike. We have a fix in review.

[02:02] Evan: Great. On Commercial, Maya?

[02:06] Maya: Pipeline healthy, a few large deals moved from eval to pilot. We're seeing more customers ask about Dedicated and Private for compliance, especially healthcare and finance. Pricing asks are around committed capacity with predictable cost. We'll share a standard pilot template later this week.

[02:30] Maya: Also want to call out a competitor mention — Anthropic's enterprise offering is being evaluated by some prospects; teams are asking about our model catalog and verified performance profiles.

[02:48] Evan: Good to know. Priya, product roadmap?

[02:52] Priya: Ok roadmap high level — Q2 focus: 1) model lifecycle features: version pinning, rollout policies, automatic fallback; 2) Optimize: smarter quantization recommendations and batching configs exposed in console; 3) security: KMS/HSM integrations and expanded audit logs for Private. We'll open a public RFC for the rollout policies next week.

[03:25] Priya: For model onboarding we plan a gallery of validated models with performance profiles — it's half-survey, half-benchmark. Expect the first set within three weeks.

[03:45] Oliver: UX note — we'll add a dedicated rollout page with canary percentage sliders, history, and rollback buttons, aiming for clear operational affordances.

[04:05] Evan: Sounds good. On Private and Dedicated launches — status? Daniel?

[04:12] Daniel: Dedicated GA is on track for late May. We've got two pilot customers in dedicated pools and the autoscaling changes are stable in staging. Private (VPC) has one on-prem pilot; networking edge cases popped up — BGP routes and firewall rules were less consistent across customer infra, so we built a preflight checklist.

[04:40] Employee 2: For Private, what about KMS support for on-prem HSM? Is that roadmap item going to include HSM certs?

[04:48] Priya: Yes, HSM integration is Q2 stretch. We'll support cloud KMS first then HSM options in the next quarter. We'll post a compliance matrix with supported KMS providers.

[05:15] Evan: On SLOs and SLAs, customers ask for latency guarantees. We offer SLO guidance for hosted but for Dedicated/Private we need a clearer mapping. Daniel will collaborate with Product to publish realistic latency ranges per pool type.

[05:38] Daniel: Yep, we'll include example p95/p99 numbers across sequence lengths and model families.

[05:50] Evan: Ok hiring — People Ops? Quick update from Lina out of band — we're adding 18 hires in Q2 across infra, SE, and sales. We'll do two hiring all hands next week focused on interview calibration.

[06:14] Employee 3: Is there an update on the eng org changes?

[06:20] Evan: We'll share an org chart after this meeting — Daniel will outline team ownership for runtime vs orchestration. Daniel?

[06:28] Daniel: We're splitting the serving runtime team into Core Runtime and Deployment Platform. Core Runtime focuses on kernel selection, batching, quantization; Deployment Platform handles autoscaling, routing, and private deployment integration. This should reduce merge conflicts and make on-call more focused.

[06:52] Priya: A note on metrics — product will publish a public performance dashboard internally: token cost trends, model latency heatmaps, and failed requests by route. It's internal but intended to help sales and CSMs qualify.

[07:12] Maya: Sales ops — reminder that new pricing tiers go live May 1 for new customers, existing customers get grandfathering for 90 days. Account teams will get a script and FAQ.

[07:34] Evan: Quick finance check — burn is within plan but we need to be careful on GPU fleet growth. We're optimizing per-token economics. Priya and Daniel, please prioritize the quantization and caching recommendations that have the highest unit-cost impact.

[07:55] Daniel: On caching, the prefix/KV cache improvements reduced repeated-context calls by 20% in our bench. We're moving that into canary this week.

[08:10] Employee 4: question about audits — SOC2 timeline?

[08:15] Evan: SOC 2 Type II audit is scheduled for Q3. Security team is collecting controls evidence now. We will have an FAQ for customers on controls and logs.

[08:33] Priya: Another product note — we're adding structured output templates and first-class function-calling examples in SDKs, aim is to reduce customer prompt engineering time.

[08:50] Evan: Alright going into Q&A, please add questions to chat; we'll take as many as we can.

[09:05] Employee 5: For Dedicated do we have explicit price per GPU or is it still a committed vCPU/GPU unit?

[09:12] Maya: It's committed capacity by GPU-pool unit. We'll publish the pricing matrix after legal signs off.

[09:30] Employee 6: Any change to data residency — EU customers asking about data locality?

[09:36] Priya: We're expanding region coverage and will support EU-only data processing for Private deployments; Hosted customers can set region flags for routing. We'll add a data residency page.

[09:58] Evan: Final recap — Priya will share the roadmap doc by Apr 15, Daniel to share infra capacity plan by Apr 12, Maya will distribute sales pilot template this week. Recording and slides posted by EOD. Action items in the doc. Thanks everyone.

[10:20] (meeting ends, small chatter and people leaving)

Notes on transcription: auto-transcript had a few misheard terms (nv-interop sometimes 'nv inter op'), and speaker labels are generic for some attendees. Links shared: slides: https://redwood.company/slides/apr-2026-allhands (internal), roadmap RFC: https://redwood.company/rfcs/rollout-policies (internal).
